title: Jonathon Cooper, facing felony assault charge, practices with Broncos as camp begins
content:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. — Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper, who is facing a felony assault charge and other charges related to a pair of offseason incidents with his then-girlfriend, practiced with the team Wednesday during its first of two acclimation workouts ahead of Friday’s official start of training camp.

It is the first time Cooper has been on the field since being excused by the team from its June minicamp following the second of two arrests in Douglas County (Colo.). The first occurred June 4 and ultimately resulted in Cooper being charged with assault by strangulation, a second-degree felony. He was arrested again June 12 on suspicion of violating a protective order stemming from the first incident. He is next scheduled to appear in court for an arraignment hearing Aug. 31, three days after Denver’s final game of the preseason. His case is under review by the NFL, a league spokesman told The Athletic.

Broncos coach Sean Payton said Wednesday that the Broncos are “staying the course with league protocol and club protocol, relative to what we’re advised to do.” He said he, general manager George Paton and owner Greg Penner all met with Cooper about the June incidents, and that the veteran linebacker was “fantastic” the past six weeks as he worked away from the building.

“We’re supportive, and yet I’m very much aware of the seriousness of these types of things,” Payton said. “Pretty much what I said in the spring (is) there’s a schedule and a course to this, and that’s what we have to follow.”

The felony assault charge for Cooper stems from an incident at his apartment June 4 and resulted, in part, from a forensic nurse’s report about Cooper’s then-girlfriend following a physical altercation. The nurse wrote at the time that the woman suffered “serious bodily injury” that was consistent with “strangulation with hypoxia” and “traumatic brain injury,” according to an arrest affidavit. The woman alleged, according to the affidavit, that Cooper grabbed her by the throat and picked her up, adding she “struggled to breathe” during the incident.

Payton on Wednesday declined to address the specifics of the allegations against Cooper, including those outlined in the nurse’s report.

“I read all of it and, listen, I don’t have any comment on the specifics because I think, yeah, when it’s finally finished, we’ll have a better feel,” Payton said, referring to the ongoing legal process and the league’s investigation. “It’s unfair for me to answer any of those questions right now without having the totality of it finalized, and I think it’ll come sooner rather than later.”

While NFL investigations often rely on information that arises during legal proceedings, a player does not have to be convicted of a violent crime or plead guilty to one to be subject to a suspension under the league’s personal conduct policy.

The policy states: “An individual is subject to discipline under the policy if the person is determined to be guilty of a criminal charge or if the NFL investigation demonstrates the person engaged in conduct prohibited by the policy.”

Violations involving assault, the policy states, will result in a baseline six-game suspension without pay.

The team decided to keep Cooper away from the field during minicamp, but Payton suggested Wednesday the Broncos are now allowing the NFL’s investigative process to set the course.

“There’s a process with the league relative to the legal process,” Payton said. “And then, as that all comes together, we can make the right decision. And that’s simply it. There’s no follow-ups. There’s no other underlying — it’s just today’s protocol. And there’s probably, maybe, players in other camps that are kinda going through a similar protocol. And, man, we’re proud of the work he did, call it this last month, month and a half. (It) wasn’t easy and it’ll continue to be a challenge, and we’ll see where it goes. But fully supportive of him right now as we gather all the information and we go from there.”

Cooper, a seventh-round pick by the Broncos in the 2021 NFL Draft, is entering his sixth NFL season. He has 31.5 career sacks, 18.5 of which have come over the past two seasons.
